site.title: Andrés Atencio — Software Developer · IT Teacher
site.description: Software developer and IT teacher in Buenos Aires, with around fifteen years of professional software experience and current work in technology education.

paragraphs: I’m a software developer and IT teacher based in Buenos Aires. I spent around fifteen years working professionally on web and mobile software, and today I teach information technology while continuing to build and maintain software for educational, institutional and personal projects.

My work has moved across different technologies, products and learning environments, but the underlying practice is much the same: understand a system, make useful changes, solve concrete problems and explain technical ideas clearly.

experience.heading: Experience
paragraphs: My professional software career spans roughly fifteen years, from business and logistics systems to mobile content platforms and web and mobile products. Since late 2023, teaching has become my main professional activity, while software development continues through educational, institutional and personal work.

roles.description: I worked on web and desktop applications, including logistics and distribution systems. The work was mainly in the Microsoft ecosystem, with C#, ASP.NET, Visual Basic and SQL Server.

I spent almost seven years working on web and mobile systems for subscription, distribution and download of digital content. My work during this period included Android/Java as well as C#, ASP.NET, Angular and SQL Server.

I worked on web and mobile products across domains including surveys, healthcare and online communities, collaborating with distributed teams in English. Different projects involved technologies such as JavaScript and TypeScript, React, Node.js, Python, Ruby on Rails, PostgreSQL and Flutter/Dart.

currentDevelopment.heading: Current development
paragraphs: Since moving into teaching as my main activity, I have continued developing software in educational, institutional and personal contexts.

items.heading: Institutional tools
paragraphs: Small systems built around real institutional needs, including a bulletin-generation tool maintained over time.

items.heading: Educational software
paragraphs: Software and web projects created for classes and technical training, combining development practice with teaching.

items.heading: This site
paragraphs: This site is part of my current development work: a versioned static project built with Astro and TypeScript.

teaching.heading: Teaching and technology education
paragraphs: I currently teach Information Technology in secondary schools in Buenos Aires City and work as an IT instructor and vocational-training reference at CFP No. 7.
I plan and develop my own materials and teach programming, web interfaces, HTML, CSS, GitHub and publication through practical projects.
From 2019 to 2020, while working in software, I also taught introductory programming, persistence and user interfaces in UNAHUR’s University Programming Technician program.

items.heading: Systems
paragraphs: I earned the intermediate degree of Systems Information Analyst at Universidad del Salvador, after studying there from 2015 to 2017 while working at Mobile Streams.

items.heading: Teaching
paragraphs: I’m currently completing pedagogical training for professionals and higher-level technicians at IES Juan B. Justo, with 12 of 15 course units completed.

items.heading: Broader study
paragraphs: Before completing my systems qualification, I also studied Veterinary Medicine, Literature and Biology teacher education. Those paths were not completed as degrees, but they remain part of my broader academic background.

workingTogether.heading: Working together
paragraphs: I’m interested in part-time, remote-friendly software work, particularly when collaboration can be largely asynchronous and responsibilities are clear.

A small, well-defined piece of work on an existing system is a natural way to start — understanding a codebase, fixing or extending functionality, working with data or APIs, and debugging concrete problems. I’m open to contractor or freelance arrangements.

contact.heading: Contact
paragraphs: If you think my background might fit something you’re working on, feel free to get in touch.
